findings.passage: “Asking somebody to prove they are a citizen and a resident is not asking too much,” Moul said. “So when somebody says that’s voter suppression – we will give you free IDs in Pennsylvania. We will give them to you free of charge. If you cannot afford to buy one, one will be provided for you. I don’t buy into that voter suppression one iota. It is a narrative pushed by the left.”
findings.note: Quoted by Gettysburg Connection (date is the article's publish date) after the governor vetoed House Bill 1300, which would have required ID at every election. He speaks to ID, proof of being a citizen and resident, and free IDs.

findings.passage: “Voter suppression is a lie,” Moul said. “I mean, I don’t know how else– I call things the way I see them, but when somebody says that asking for ID is voter suppression, it is a lie. It’s a narrative they can fall back on for people that are less intelligent to believe. We have people that will believe this lie because they’ve been spoon-fed this.”
findings.note: Quoted by Gettysburg Connection on whether asking for ID is voter suppression.

findings.passage: “It allowed drop boxes, but not drop boxes set up on street corners that anyone could get access to,” Moul said. “They’d be in controlled, secured areas.”
findings.note: Quoted by Gettysburg Connection on what House Bill 1300 allowed for ballot drop boxes.

findings.passage: “You almost have to, because if these guys are going to use their corruptness to taint whatever we do, or change whatever we do, you have no choice but to take it to the people as a referendum for the constitution,” he said.
findings.note: Quoted by Gettysburg Connection on taking election rule changes to a statewide ballot referendum after the veto.
